group.title: Travel
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A detailed plan of a trip, with places and times.
examples: Our {itinerary} includes three cities in five days.
wrong: An itinerary is a bag that you carry on a plane.

words.meaning: A document that allows you to get on a plane.
examples: Show your {boarding pass} at the gate.
wrong: A boarding pass is a ticket for a meal in a hotel.

words.meaning: A short stop between two flights on a long journey.
examples: We had a three-hour {layover} in Dubai.
wrong: A layover is the last night of a trip at home.

words.meaning: An official stamp or document that allows you to enter or stay in a country.
examples: You need a {visa} to work in that country.
wrong: A visa is a card that you use to rent a hotel room for free.

words.meaning: A place to stay, such as a hotel or an apartment.
examples: The price includes {accommodation} and breakfast.
wrong: Accommodation is the food that you eat on a flight.

words.meaning: The process of reporting your arrival at an airport or a hotel.
examples: {Check-in} opens two hours before the flight.
wrong: Check-in is the final step before you leave a hotel.

words.meaning: Visiting interesting places as a tourist.
examples: We spent the day {sightseeing} in the old town.
wrong: Sightseeing is the act of sleeping in a hotel all day.

words.meaning: The money used in a particular country.
examples: The local {currency} is the euro.
wrong: Currency is a document that gives you permission to travel.

words.meaning: The value of one country’s money compared with another’s.
examples: The {exchange rate} changes every day.
wrong: An exchange rate is the price of a train ticket.

words.meaning: The money you pay to travel on a bus, train or plane.
examples: The bus {fare} is two dollars.
wrong: A fare is a fast train that does not stop.

words.meaning: A short trip taken for pleasure, often with a group.
examples: We took an {excursion} to the island.
wrong: An excursion is a long delay at an airport.

words.meaning: A cheap place to stay where guests often share rooms.
examples: We stayed in a {hostel} near the station.
wrong: A hostel is an expensive restaurant on the top of a hill.

words.meaning: A journey to a place and back again.
examples: A {round trip} ticket is cheaper than two one-way tickets.
wrong: A round trip is a journey that only goes in one direction.

words.meaning: Allowing travel in only one direction.
examples: I bought a {one-way} ticket to Chicago.
wrong: A one-way ticket is a ticket for a trip there and back.

words.meaning: A change from one vehicle or route to another during a journey.
examples: The trip needs a {transfer} at the central station.
wrong: A transfer is a trip that never stops anywhere.

words.meaning: A building at an airport where passengers begin or end a flight.
examples: Our flight leaves from {terminal} two.
wrong: A terminal is a small bag for carrying your passport.

words.meaning: Tiredness caused by flying across several time zones.
examples: It took me three days to recover from {jet lag}.
wrong: Jet lag is a kind of delay caused by bad weather.

words.meaning: A book with information for people visiting a place.
examples: The {guidebook} lists the best cafes in town.
wrong: A guidebook is a ticket for the last train of the night.

words.meaning: A building or place that is easy to recognize and well known.
examples: The tower is the city’s most famous {landmark}.
wrong: A landmark is a small bag that tourists carry.

words.meaning: An arrangement to receive money if something is lost, damaged or stolen.
examples: Travel {insurance} covers lost luggage.
wrong: Insurance is a ticket that lets you skip the line at an airport.

words.meaning: A list of the times when trains, buses or flights leave and arrive.
examples: Check the {timetable} before you go to the station.
wrong: A timetable is a ticket that lets you enter a museum.

words.meaning: A small bag that you take with you on a plane.
examples: My {carry-on} fits under the seat.
wrong: A carry-on is a bag that you must give to the airline staff before you board.

words.meaning: A room in a hotel that is free for guests.
examples: The sign said there was no {vacancy} on Friday.
wrong: A vacancy is a hotel room that is full of guests.

words.meaning: A long journey, especially by sea.
examples: The {voyage} to the island took six days.
wrong: A voyage is a short walk to the shop on the corner.

words.meaning: A vacation on a large ship that visits several places.
examples: They took a {cruise} around the Caribbean.
wrong: A cruise is a trip on a plane that never lands.

words.meaning: A place where people go for a vacation, with hotels and activities.
examples: We stayed at a beach {resort} for a week.
wrong: A resort is an office where tourists pay for their visas.

words.meaning: A small room on a ship, or the passenger area of a plane.
examples: Our {cabin} had two small beds.
wrong: A cabin is a large hall where the whole crew sleeps.

words.meaning: The time by which guests must leave a hotel room.
examples: {Check-out} is at eleven in the morning.
wrong: Check-out is the moment when you first enter your hotel room.

words.meaning: A person who shows visitors around a place and explains it.
examples: The {tour guide} told us about the history of the castle.
wrong: A tour guide is a tourist who gets lost on purpose.
